section1.title: Why a game beats a film night when you want to reconnect
section1.p1: A couple game looks like nothing much, and yet it solves a very concrete problem: as a couple you always end up telling each other about the same day in the same words. A game breaks that pattern because it asks the questions for you. Nobody has to find the courage to raise a subject, the card does it.
section1.p2: That is also why a game works better than a film when you want to find each other again. In front of a screen, you are two people side by side looking at the same thing. Around a game, you are two people looking at each other. The difference sounds slight, and it changes everything after an hour.
section1.p3: Every game on this page is played online, free, on a single phone set down between you. No account to create, no app to install, nothing to print. You pick, you open, you play.

section2.title: Which game to pick, depending on the moment
section2.intro: That is the real question, and it depends far less on your taste than on the moment you are in. Here is how we would sort them.
section2.row1Moment: A long drive or train journey
section2.row1Pourquoi: Nothing to look at, nothing to mime: it works by voice, without the driver leaving the road.
section2.row2Moment: An evening that is fizzling out
section2.row2Pourquoi: It takes no energy to start and it gets you laughing within three questions.
section2.row3Pourquoi: The alternating format leaves time to eat between questions, and the answers always surprise.
section2.row4Pourquoi: The only one that goes up to eight players, and the group vote is what makes it fun.
section2.row5Moment: A moment that is just the two of you
section2.row5Pourquoi: It builds up gradually, which gives each of you time to follow or to slow down.

section3.title: Making a game night for two work
section3.p1: Four things separate a game you abandon after ten minutes from an evening you are still talking about the next day.
section3.conseil1Titre: One phone, set down between you
section3.conseil1Texte: Two screens means two attentions elsewhere. All our games are built to run on a single device you pass back and forth, and it completely changes the evening.
section3.conseil2Texte: One notification is enough to break a moment that was just getting interesting. It is the most obvious advice on this list and by far the most effective.
section3.conseil3Titre: The right to skip a turn
section3.conseil3Texte: A game for two only works if nobody feels trapped. Agree from the start that either of you can decline a question without justifying it, and you will paradoxically go much further.
section3.conseil4Texte: The classic mistake is opening with the boldest game. Start with something light: the rest follows on its own once the laughing has started.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.q1: Are these couple games really free?
faq.a1: Yes, every one of them. There is no account to create, no paid tier, no content unlocked after payment. You open the game page and you play, from a phone or a computer.
faq.q2: Do I need to download an app?
faq.a2: No. Everything runs directly in your browser. That is also what lets you start a game in ten seconds when the urge strikes, without going through an app store or using up storage on your phone.
faq.q3: What is the best couple game to play at home?
faq.a3: It depends what you are after. To laugh, the funny quiz. To discover each other, the questions to ask or the mutual knowledge game. To spice up the evening, the spicy quiz. The table above sorts the games by moment rather than by theme, which is the more useful ranking in practice.
faq.q4: Can we play remotely, each at home?
faq.a4: Yes, most work well over video or a phone call: one of you opens the game, reads out loud and records the answers. The question games lend themselves particularly well to it. We also have a quiz designed specifically for long distance couples.
faq.q5: Are these games suitable for a couple who have just met?
faq.a5: Some are made for exactly that. The questions to ask and the funny quiz work from the first weeks, because they assume no shared history. Games that ask you to guess the other person's answers are more fun after a few months.

section4.title: A game repairs nothing, but it opens doors
section4.p1: Let us be honest about what a game can do. It does not settle a fundamental disagreement and it does not replace a real conversation when one is needed. What it does very well is create the occasion for that conversation, in a light setting where nobody feels summoned.
section4.p2: And if you want to go further than one evening, our couple tests raise the same subjects with a result at the end.
